question.problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{16}({x}^{3}+{y}^{3}),\, & 0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{13}{10}$ and $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{13}{10},$ calculate the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
The covariance of $X$ and $Y$ can be calculated using the formula

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]=\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y].
$$

To find $\text{E}[XY],$ we use the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}xyf(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}xy\cdot \frac{1}{16}({x}^{3}+{y}^{3})\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{16}y{\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{4}+x{y}^{3})\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{16}y{[\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}{y}^{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{16}y[\frac{32}{5}+2{y}^{3}]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{2}{5}y+\frac{1}{8}{y}^{4})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{1}{5}{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{40}{y}^{5}]}_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =\frac{8}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the covariance formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{8}{5}-(\frac{13}{10})(\frac{13}{10}) \\  & =-\frac{9}{100}.\end{aligned}
$$
